expectations.text: The reply opens with a recommendation against cutting every cost centre by 8% and explains why a blanket cut lands mostly on payroll and cuts efficient and wasteful areas alike.
expectations.evidence: The reply opens: "**My recommendation: don't take the flat 8% to the board.**" It then explains: "Payroll is 68% of opex, so 'every cost centre cuts 8%' turns into about 48 FTE leaving." Memo section 2: "An 8% cut there is 48 FTE (est.) and falls on the efficient and the bloated alike."

expectations.text: The reply establishes which number the board actually needs (cash, margin or a covenant) and by when, and sizes the gap in money or shows how to.
expectations.evidence: Number and timing: "Is it an in-year or a Q4 run-rate target?" and "What is it for: margin, a covenant, a valuation? ... If a covenant is involved, we need a 13-week cash forecast and an early talk with the bank." Memo section 12 asks the board to "Restate the target: baseline, in-year versus run-rate, and purpose." Gap: "8% is EUR 6.0M, roughly twice your whole margin" (8% x 75M is correct). Caveat: the indexation add-on is attributed to the wrong baseline reading (see factual_errors). The core gap is still sized correctly.

expectations.text: The reply works the levers that cost no jobs first (such as vendors, licences, cloud, office, consultants, pricing or revenue leakage) and estimates what they close or shows how to size them.
expectations.evidence: "Zero-base the EUR 24M non-payroll spend: subcontractors, licences, travel, facilities. I sized about 12%, EUR 2.85M run-rate (EUR 1.96M in 2027)." The memo itemises subcontractors 1.2, IT and licences 0.48, travel/marketing 0.45, facilities 0.32 and other 0.40, which sum to 2.85. Pricing: "+3% on 40% of revenue is about EUR 0.9M margin" (0.03 x 0.4 x 78 = 0.94). Utilisation: "each point on about 450 billable FTE is roughly EUR 0.8M".

expectations.text: The reply handles headcount through flows (a hiring freeze with exceptions, natural attrition, internal moves) rather than cuts, and protects named investments with explicit criteria.
expectations.evidence: Flows: "Hiring freeze with exceptions: leave 25 non-billable or bench roles open as people leave. Expected attrition is 72 leavers at 12%." Memo section 7: "Freeze with exceptions for billable roles and critical skills ... moves from bench to billable roles first. No involuntary reductions in the base plan." Protection: "Training, security, quality and customer-facing capacity are not in the list. Cutting them is booked with its future cost (rehiring EUR 30-60k per leaver, quality incidents, lost renewals) beside the saving. Billable roles are only left open when utilisation data shows bench."

expectations.text: The reply puts leaders' pay, bonuses or perks on the table before other people's jobs.
expectations.evidence: "Leaders first: the leadership team takes the first and largest cut, bonus pool and a temporary pay reduction, about EUR 0.5M." Memo section 8: "announced before any wider measure". Board decision 3: "Approve leaders-first measures." The base plan has no involuntary job losses.

expectations.text: The reply gives the board a usable structure: levers with amount, timing, owner and confidence, what stops or waits, and any gap that remains.
expectations.evidence: Memo section 4 table columns: "2027 net | Run-rate | Lands in | Owner | Confidence | Human impact". The totals add up (1.96+1.06+0.38+0.50-0.25 = 3.65; 2.85+2.13+0.60 = 5.58). Section 6, "What stops or waits": "Two internal programmes ..., non-essential travel, new office fit-outs, discretionary consultancy and licences with under-30% use." Gap: "EUR 0.42M run-rate (EUR 2.35M in-year)", which matches 6.0-5.58 and 6.0-3.65. The memo also has a trigger table and a list of board decisions.

overall_quality.evidence: A clear, quantified and honest plan with a sound end-Q2 gate and leaders going first, but it gets the wage-indexation baseline effect backwards, which a CFO would catch in the board pre-read.

factual_errors.evidence: 1) It says that measuring the 8% against 'the 2027 baseline after CAO/wage indexation' adds EUR 1.5-2.0M to the gap. It's the other way round: a target of 8% below 2026 actuals forces the company to absorb indexation as well (adds ~1.5-2.0M), while a post-indexation baseline already contains it (adds only ~0.14M). Checked and correct: works council mandatory from 50; art. 25 WOR advice before the decision is final; WMCO at 20+ in one UWV area within three months; transition payment ~2.3 months at 7 years' service (1/3 month per year); Trevor & Nyberg.

skill_leak.evidence: No mention of skills, reference files, 'cost ladder' or 'rungs'. 'critical skills' refers to staff skills.

owns_result.evidence: No bad outcome is part of the prompt: the margin is thin but positive and the board has set a target, so this check doesn't apply. A has the leadership team take 'the first and largest cut' but never says the result is leadership's responsibility.

best_insight.value: It asks the board to instruct management to involve the works council now, whatever is decided, and sets a quantified end-Q2 gate (delivered savings below 70% of plan) that opens voluntary exits and redeployment before any involuntary step.

suggestions.assertion: The reply establishes which number the board actually needs (cash, margin or a covenant) and by when, and sizes the gap in money or shows how to.
suggestions.reason: Every sample passes by asking 'what is the 8% for?' and 'in-year or run-rate?'. Asking the question is enough to pass, so the assertion doesn't separate the samples. It never checks whether the baseline/indexation effect is stated in the right direction (sample A gets it backwards) or whether the plan shows how it changes under each answer.

No assertion checks whether temporary savings (leader pay or bonus cuts, a delayed pay review) are kept out of the exit run-rate. B, C and E count leader cuts in the run-rate to get close to 8%, while A and D exclude them correctly. That difference matters to a board.

No assertion checks that lever amounts, quarterly timing and the stated gap agree with each other. Sample E's largest lever shows the same figure in-year and at exit while ramping quarterly; only arithmetic checking catches that.

suggestions.assertion: The reply handles headcount through flows (a hiring freeze with exceptions, natural attrition, internal moves) rather than cuts, and protects named investments with explicit criteria.
suggestions.reason: This bundles two tests (flows instead of cuts, and protected investments with criteria). Splitting them would make failures easier to read; 'explicit criteria' is also loose enough that naming categories plus 'book the future cost' passes.

eval_feedback.overall: Passes all six. The assertions don't catch the reversed indexation-baseline claim, which is the sample's main analytical flaw.
